summary: A young girl married off by her mother or brothers may do mi'un, saying she does not want the marriage. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about when and how she may do it.
stIntro: The Sages decreed that in the case of a minor girl whose father died, her mother or brothers may marry her off. However, such a marriage does not have the same legal status as the marriage of an adult. Therefore, if the minor regrets having married, she is allowed to make a declaration of refusal to her husband, thereby annulling the marital bond. The Sages disagreed with regard to the details of this halakha:

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: only engaged girls may do mi'un.
chunks.st: Only betrothed girls may refuse.
chunks.stMore: A girl may refuse, upon reaching adulthood, to remain married to the man to whom her mother or brothers married her as a minor after the death of her father.

words.note: A young girl saying "I do not want this husband," which ends the marriage.

chunks.st: at her husband and not at her yavam. In such a situation, she must perform ḥalitza in order to dissolve the levirate bond.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: But Beit Hillel say: It may be directed

chunks.st: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:

chunks.en: "She may do mi'un while she is young,
chunks.st: She may refuse as long as she is a minor,

chunks.en: Rather, she does mi'un and waits until she grows up,

summary: Which young girl needs to do mi'un? One who was married off with her agreement. Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Eliezer say some girls do not need mi'un at all.

chunks.en: Which young girl needs to do mi'un?
chunks.st: Who is a minor girl who needs to perform refusal in order to annul her marriage?

chunks.en: Any whose mother and brothers married her off with her agreement.
chunks.st: Any minor whose mother or brother married her off with her consent.

chunks.en: If they married her off without her agreement,
chunks.st: If they married her off without her consent,

chunks.en: she does not need to do mi'un.
chunks.st: she need not refuse her husband at all and may leave her husband without a declaration of refusal.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Antignos says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:

chunks.he: כָּל תִּינוֹקֶת שֶׁאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לִשְׁמֹר קִדּוּשֶׁיהָ,
chunks.en: any little girl who cannot take care of her kiddushin
chunks.st: Any girl who is so young that she cannot keep her betrothal, i.e., the money or document of betrothal,

chunks.en: does not need to do mi'un.
chunks.st: safe does not need to refuse, as the Sages instituted marriage only for a girl old enough to understand what she is doing.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: what a young girl does is nothing;
chunks.st: The act of a minor girl is nothing, so that if a minor girl’s mother or brothers marry her off, the marriage is essentially invalid.

chunks.en: she is like a girl who was not really married.
chunks.st: Rather, her status is as though she were a seduced unmarried woman.

chunks.en: A Jewish girl married to a Kohen
chunks.st: Therefore, a minor daughter of a non-priest married to a priest

chunks.st: may not eat teruma,

chunks.en: A Kohen's daughter married to a regular Jew
chunks.st: and the minor daughter of a priest married to an Israelite

chunks.en: may eat terumah.
chunks.st: may eat teruma.

chunks.en: is as if she is not his wife.
chunks.st: it is as if she were not his wife. This statement will be explained in the Gemara.

summary: Mi'un undoes the marriage, so she is not like a divorced woman. A get makes her divorced. The mishnah gives a rule about which one came last.

chunks.en: A girl who does mi'un to a man:
chunks.st: If a minor girl refuses a man,

chunks.en: he is allowed to her relatives,
chunks.st: he is permitted to marry her close relatives, such as her mother or her sister,

chunks.en: and she is allowed to his relatives,
chunks.st: and she is permitted to marry his close relatives, such as his father or brother,

chunks.en: and he did not make her unfit to marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: and he has not disqualified her from marrying into the priesthood, as she is not considered divorced. However, if

chunks.en: If he gave her a get,
chunks.st: he gave her a bill of divorce, then even though the marriage was valid according to rabbinic law and not Torah law,

chunks.en: he is forbidden to her relatives,
chunks.st: he is prohibited from marrying her close relatives,

chunks.en: and she is forbidden to his relatives,
chunks.st: and she is prohibited from marrying his close relatives,

chunks.en: and he made her unfit to marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: and he has disqualified her from marrying into the priesthood.

chunks.en: If he gave her a get and took her back,
chunks.st: If he gave her a bill of divorce but afterward remarried her, and she subsequently

chunks.en: and she did mi'un and married another man
chunks.st: refused him and married another man,

chunks.en: and was widowed or divorced,
chunks.st: and then she was widowed or divorced from her second husband,

chunks.en: she may go back to him.
chunks.st: she is permitted to return to him.
chunks.stMore: Since she left him the last time by means of refusal, the refusal cancels the bill of divorce that he gave her previously, and her status is that of a minor girl who refused her husband, who is not forbidden to her first husband after a second marriage. However, if the order was different, and

chunks.en: If she did mi'un and he took her back,
chunks.st: if she refused him and he subsequently remarried her, and

chunks.en: and he gave her a get, and she married
chunks.st: this time he gave her a bill of divorce and she married

chunks.en: another man and was widowed or divorced,
chunks.st: another man, and she was widowed or divorced,

chunks.en: she may not go back to him.
chunks.st: she is forbidden to return to him, like any divorced woman who married another man.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle concerning a minor girl who refused her husband and then married several times:

chunks.en: a get after mi'un —
chunks.st: If the bill of divorce followed the refusal and she remarried,

chunks.en: she may not go back to him.
chunks.st: she is forbidden to return to him.

chunks.en: Mi'un after a get —
chunks.st: If the refusal followed the bill of divorce,

chunks.en: she may go back to him.
chunks.st: she is permitted to return to him.
chunks.stMore: Since the refusal followed the bill of divorce it is clear that she was a minor and neither the marriage nor the divorce were valid by Torah law. However, when the ultimate separation is by means of a bill of divorce, there is no indication that she was a minor at the time and there is potential for confusion with an adult divorcée.

summary: A young girl who married several men, leaving some with mi'un and some with a get, may go back to the ones she left with mi'un, but not to the ones she left with a get.

chunks.en: A girl who did mi'un to a man, and married another who divorced her,
chunks.st: If a minor girl refuses one man and marries another, and he divorces her,

chunks.en: then another, and she did mi'un,
chunks.st: and then she marries another man and refuses him,

chunks.en: then another, who divorced her,
chunks.st: and then she marries another man and he divorces her,

chunks.en: anyone she left with a get,
chunks.st: anyone she leaves by means of a bill of divorce,

chunks.en: she may not go back to him.
chunks.st: it is prohibited for her to return to him. With regard to anyone she leaves

chunks.en: With mi'un, she may go back to him.
chunks.st: by means of refusal, she is permitted to return to him.

summary: A man who divorced his wife and took her back, then died: she may do yibum, but Rabbi Eliezer forbids it. The mishnah also discusses a young girl married off by her father and then divorced.

chunks.en: Someone who divorces a woman and takes her back:
chunks.st: With regard to one who divorces a woman and remarries her and then dies childless, his wife

chunks.en: she is allowed to the yavam,
chunks.st: is permitted to enter into levirate marriage with her yavam,

chunks.en: but Rabbi Eliezer forbids.
chunks.st: but Rabbi Elazar prohibits this.

chunks.en: And so too, someone who divorces a young orphan girl and takes her back:
chunks.st: Likewise, with regard to one who divorces an orphaned minor girl whose mother and brothers married her off and remarries her and subsequently dies,

chunks.en: she is allowed to the yavam,
chunks.st: she is permitted to the yavam in levirate marriage,

chunks.en: but Rabbi Eliezer forbids.
chunks.st: and Rabbi Elazar prohibits it.

chunks.en: A young girl whose father married her off, and she was divorced,
chunks.st: A minor girl whose father married her off, in which case the marriage is valid by Torah law, and who was subsequently divorced while she was still a minor

chunks.en: is like an orphan while her father is alive.
chunks.explain: Her father can no longer marry her off.
chunks.st: is like an orphan during the lifetime of her father, as he no longer has the right to marry her off, and she cannot become fully married because she is a minor. And if the husband

chunks.en: If he took her back, everyone agrees
chunks.st: remarries her while she is still a minor and then dies childless, everyone agrees that

chunks.en: she is forbidden to the yavam.
chunks.st: she is forbidden to the yavam and may not enter into levirate marriage.

summary: Two brothers married two sisters who were young orphans. If one husband dies, his widow is his brother's wife's sister. The Tannaim argue what to do when the widow is grown up but the wife is still young.

chunks.en: Two brothers married to two
chunks.st: If two brothers are married to two minor

chunks.en: sisters who were young orphans,
chunks.st: sisters,

chunks.en: and the husband of one of them died:
chunks.st: and the husband of one of them dies childless,

chunks.en: she goes out because she is his wife's sister.
chunks.st: this widowed girl shall be exempt from levirate marriage due to her status as a forbidden relative, as one is prohibited from marrying the sister of his wife.

chunks.en: And so too with two deaf-mute sisters, or a grown one and a young one:
chunks.st: The same halakha applies to two deaf-mute women, whose status is like that of two minors in this matter, as their marriages are valid by rabbinic law. And if two brothers were married to two sisters, one of them an adult and the other a minor, and

chunks.en: if the young one's husband died,
chunks.st: the husband of the minor dies,

chunks.en: the young one goes out because she is his wife's sister.
chunks.st: the minor shall leave due to her status as the sister of a wife, as in the first case in the mishna. But

chunks.en: If the grown one's husband died,
chunks.st: if the husband of the adult dies, it generates a Torah obligation of levirate marriage, which is not abrogated by the rabbinic prohibition proscribing the yevama as his wife’s sister.
chunks.stMore: This prohibition is by rabbinic law, because marriage to a minor is rabbinic in origin. What does one do under such circumstances?

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: we teach the young one to do mi'un to him.
chunks.explain: Then he may do yibum with her grown sister.
chunks.st: We instruct the minor, i.e., his wife, to refuse him, so that her marriage is dissolved and he may then enter into levirate marriage with her adult sister, the widow of his childless brother.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel says:

chunks.en: if she did mi'un,
chunks.st: If the minor refuses of her own accord,

chunks.en: then she did mi'un. And if not,
chunks.st: her refusal is valid. And if not,

chunks.en: she waits until she grows up,
chunks.st: she should wait until she reaches majority, whereupon her marriage is valid by Torah law,

chunks.en: and the other goes out because she is his wife's sister.
chunks.st: and that widowed adult sister shall be exempt from levirate marriage due to her status as the sister of a wife.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says: When the brother married to the adult sister dies, leaving the brother married to the minor,

chunks.en: "Woe to him for his wife,
chunks.st: woe [ee] to him for his wife,

chunks.en: and woe to him for his brother's wife!"
chunks.st: woe to him for his brother’s wife. Under these circumstances, he loses both women:

chunks.en: He sends away his wife with a get,
chunks.st: He must release his own wife with a bill of divorce and

chunks.en: and his brother's wife with chalitzah.
chunks.st: his brother’s wife by performing ḥalitza.
chunks.stMore: He cannot stay married to his wife because she is the sister of his yevama, and he cannot enter into levirate marriage with the yevama even after divorcing his wife, because the yevama is his wife’s sister. The principle that one is completely absolved from levirate marriage when the potential yevama is a forbidden relative does not apply because Torah law does not recognize his marriage to his minor wife. That marriage’s rabbinic sanction does not suffice to render the yevama, his wife’s sister, a forbidden relative who is not a candidate for levirate marriage.

summary: When a man had two wives and died, yibum or chalitzah with one frees the other only if both had the same kind of marriage. A wife whose marriage is stronger frees the other, but not the other way.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁהָיָה נָשׂוּי לִשְׁתֵּי יְתוֹמוֹת קְטַנּוֹת,
chunks.en: Someone who was married to two young orphan girls
chunks.st: If a man was married to two orphaned minors

chunks.en: and died: the yibum or chalitzah of
chunks.st: and died, consummation of levirate marriage or ḥalitza with

chunks.en: one of them frees her co-wife.
chunks.st: one of them exempts her rival wife from either levirate marriage or ḥalitza, rendering her free to remarry.

chunks.en: And so with two deaf-mute women.
chunks.st: Likewise, if two deaf-mutes were married to one man who died, consummation of levirate marriage or ḥalitza with one of them exempts her rival wife.
chunks.stMore: In both of these cases, both women are married by rabbinic law and consequently become yevamot by rabbinic law. Since their statuses are equal, one can exempt the other.

chunks.en: A young girl and a deaf-mute:
chunks.st: If one wife is a minor and the other is a deaf-mute,

chunks.he: אֵין בִּיאַת אַחַת מֵהֶן פּוֹטֶרֶת צָרָתָהּ.
chunks.en: yibum with one of them does not free her co-wife.
chunks.st: consummation of levirate marriage or ḥalitza with one of them does not exempt her rival wife. Although both women are married by rabbinic law, their statuses are not the same and one cannot exempt the other.

chunks.en: One who can hear and speak and a deaf-mute:
chunks.st: If one of them was halakhically competent and one was a deaf-mute,

words.en: one who can hear and speak

chunks.en: yibum with the one who can hear frees the deaf-mute,
chunks.st: consummation of levirate marriage with the halakhically competent wife exempts the deaf-mute, as the halakhically competent women’s marriage and levirate marriage are by Torah law.

chunks.he: וְאֵין בִּיאַת הַחֵרֶשֶׁת פּוֹטֶרֶת אֶת הַפִּקַּחַת.
chunks.en: but yibum with the deaf-mute does not free the one who hears.
chunks.st: But consummation of levirate marriage with the deaf-mute does not exempt the halakhically competent wife.

chunks.en: A grown woman and a young girl:
chunks.st: Likewise, if one was an adult woman and one a minor girl,

chunks.en: yibum with the grown one frees the young one,
chunks.st: consummation of levirate marriage with the adult exempts the minor

chunks.he: וְאֵין בִּיאַת הַקְּטַנָּה פוֹטֶרֶת אֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה:
chunks.en: but yibum with the young one does not free the grown one.
chunks.st: but consummation of levirate marriage with the minor does not exempt the adult.

summary: A yavam did yibum with one widow and then wrongly with the other. Whether the first stays his wife depends on what kind of marriages the two widows had.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁהָיָה נָשׂוּי לִשְׁתֵּי יְתוֹמוֹת קְטַנּוֹת,
chunks.en: Someone who was married to two young orphan girls
chunks.st: If a man was married to two minor orphans

chunks.en: and died: if the yavam did yibum with the first,
chunks.st: and he died, and a yavam engaged in intercourse with the first of them to consummate the levirate marriage,

chunks.en: and then went back and did it with the second,
chunks.st: and then engaged in intercourse with the second,

chunks.en: or his brother did it with the second,
chunks.st: or if his brother who is also their yavam engaged in intercourse with the second, the yavam or his brother

chunks.en: he did not make the first one unfit.
chunks.st: did not disqualify the first girl from staying married to him, as her levirate marriage was consummated.

chunks.en: And so with two deaf-mute women.
chunks.st: Likewise, if the two wives were two female deaf-mutes, the first wife may remain married to the yavam.
chunks.stMore: Intercourse with the second wife, though prohibited, has no effect: If the marriage was of uncertain status, then either the levirate marriage was concluded when he engaged in intercourse with the first, or neither wife was really married to the first husband, and they are therefore not rival wives. If the initial marriage was partial, then since both wives have the same standing, the levirate marriage with the first wife fully realizes whatever degree of levirate marriage is available.

chunks.en: A young girl and a deaf-mute:
chunks.st: If one wife was a minor and the other a deaf-mute, and

chunks.en: if the yavam did yibum with the young one,
chunks.st: the yavam engaged in intercourse with the minor

chunks.en: he did not make the young one unfit.
chunks.st: then the yavam or his brother disqualified the minor from staying married due to the Sages’ decree, lest it be confused with a situation where the intercourse with the deaf-mute was first.
chunks.basisNote: Our Hebrew text says "not unfit." Steinsaltz follows the Gemara's version, "made unfit."

chunks.en: If the yavam did yibum with the deaf-mute,

chunks.st: or if his brother engaged in intercourse with the minor, then the yavam or his brother

chunks.st: disqualified the deaf-mute from staying married.
chunks.stMore: The marriage to the deaf-mute creates a partial acquisition that does not exempt the second wife from levirate marriage, as she, as a minor, has a different standing. Accordingly, intercourse with the second wife also creates a partial acquisition and thereby both women are prohibited to the yavam, as it is prohibited to consummate levirate marriage with more than one wife.

chunks.he: יָבָם קָטָן שֶׁבָּא עַל יְבָמָה קְטַנָּה,

chunks.en: If he did yibum with a grown yevamah,
chunks.st: If he engaged in sexual intercourse with an adult yevama,

chunks.he: תְּגַדְּלֶנּוּ. הַיְבָמָה שֶׁאָמְרָה בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
chunks.en: she raises him. A yevamah who said within thirty days,
chunks.st: she should raise him, i.e., they must stay married, as there is no way for him to divorce her until he reaches majority. When a yevama said within thirty days of her marriage:

chunks.en: "He did not really marry me,"
chunks.st: I have not engaged in sexual intercourse with him, the court

chunks.en: we force him to do chalitzah with her.
chunks.st: forces him to perform ḥalitza with her. If she said this

chunks.en: After thirty days,
chunks.st: after thirty days but he claimed that he had engaged in sexual intercourse, the court

chunks.en: we ask him to do chalitzah with her.
chunks.st: asks him to perform ḥalitza with her, as there are grounds to believe him.

chunks.en: And when he agrees with her,
chunks.st: And when he admits that he did not engage in intercourse with her,

chunks.en: even after twelve months
chunks.st: even after twelve months,

chunks.en: we force him to do chalitzah with her.
chunks.st: the court forces him to perform ḥalitza with her.

summary: A widow who made a neder not to get any benefit from her yavam cannot do yibum. If she made it while her husband was alive, beis din forces him to do chalitzah; if after, they only ask him.

chunks.en: A woman who makes a neder not to benefit from her yavam while her husband is alive:
chunks.st: If a woman vows during her husband’s lifetime to derive no benefit from her yavam,

chunks.en: we force him to do chalitzah with her.
chunks.st: the court forces him to perform ḥalitza with her as it is forbidden for her to engage in sexual intercourse with him to consummate the levirate marriage. If she vowed

chunks.en: After her husband died,
chunks.st: after the death of her husband to derive no benefit from her yavam, the court

chunks.en: we ask him to do chalitzah with her.
chunks.st: asks him to perform ḥalitza with her.

chunks.en: And if she meant it for this,
chunks.explain: She made the neder to get out of yibum.
chunks.st: And if she intended to do so, i.e., she had an ulterior motive of avoiding levirate marriage when she vowed,

chunks.en: even while her husband was alive,
chunks.st: even if she made the vow during her husband’s lifetime,

chunks.en: we only ask him to do chalitzah with her.
chunks.st: the court merely asks him to perform ḥalitza with her.
